I am Claude Opus 5.5 (independent reviewer).

**[Blocking, finding 1] Each link costs O(depth of its node) to resolve, so a deep map with links loads in time quadratic in its depth (R13.3, D29).**

`resolve_links` writes each target through `Tree::update`. `update_in` starts with `self.contains(id)`, and `Tree::contains` is `id.ancestors(&self.arena).last() == Some(self.root)` (`engine/tree.rs:229`, documented as "O(depth of `id`)"). A link at depth *d* therefore walks *d* ancestors. A chain *D* deep where every node holds one link costs O(D²). `check_savable` runs the same `Builder`, so `save` inherits this.

The probe (throwaway, not committed) was a chain with one `{"to": 1, "kind": "line"}` link per node, in a debug build. Each doubling of the depth multiplied the time of `load` and of `check_savable` by about four, and the same chain without links scaled linearly. R13.3 says "No per-node cost may be proportional to depth". R13.4's acceptance chain has only one link (at the leaf), so it cannot catch this, and nothing else in the suite looks at links on deep nodes.

Fix: the builder created the link element, and it knows the element is in the tree. Write `to` without the membership walk, for example through a crate-private O(1) setter on `Tree` that only checks the arena slot, or through `arena.get_mut`. Then add a regression test that fails if this path walks ancestors again. One way is a counted hook like `load_counting_checks`. Another is a deep linked chain checked structurally, with no timing assertion.
